a couple points to clean up still (pushback is also welcome)

1. “The unit of caching is a function summary” is too restrictive. Resolution, imports, type hierarchies, structural queries and module initialization don’t naturally fit that unit. Say “a named derivation with explicit inputs and outputs”, with functions and recursive groups as examples. Also distinguish a workspace-sized cache from a workspace-sized recomputation unit: the former can contain many independently invalidated entries. The retained “whole-workspace value … is too large” rule blurs that distinction. Lines 37–60

2. Memory-only derivations shouldn’t automatically require SQL dependency rows. The four-part contract currently appears to require them for every retained value. That could put SQLite writes back into the warm computation path unnecessarily. Require SQL-readable dependencies for persisted products; allow equivalent dependency tracking in memory for memory-only products. Lines 45–58

3. Make two invalidation obligations explicit.

  • Record absence and set membership, including unsuccessful lookups. Otherwise adding a previously nonexistent declaration can leave a cached miss valid.

  • Refresh dependencies even when the recomputed output digest is unchanged. Switching from provider A to B with equal output must still make later changes to B invalidate the result.

4. Make the memory budget cover retained allocations, not just cache entries. Include graph arenas, interners and dependency bookkeeping. Removing an entry while its backing arena or shared references remain alive hasn’t reclaimed its memory. This matters more now that whole-workspace retention is explicitly permitted. Lines 29–30, 67

Both reviewers found a real defect in the analysis lane's semantic-model change. When the budget could not charge the active model set, activation still reported `Ready` but cleared the analyzer's published snapshot. Later operations then silently ran without the selected models. The overlay built from those models was also measured but never charged.

The active model set is the analyzer's selected state, not an optional cache, so the budget must not be able to drop it. My fix:

- **Core:** a new `AllocationCharge::acquire_required`. It evicts cached entries to make room, then charges regardless. The budget may run over capacity while the value lives, and other admissions are refused meanwhile. A unit test covers this.
- **Runtime:** the active models and their overlay both take required charges, and the snapshot is always published again. The existing construction limit still bounds how large the model set can be.
